memories.text: The user prefers local Ollama models for generating text embeddings.
The user stores service API keys in Bitwarden Secrets Manager.
The user's vector database is a self-hosted Qdrant server.
The user prefers concise Chinese replies.
The user runs Python behavior tests with the repository's canonical test runner.
The user develops changes on separate feature branches before opening pull requests.
The user wants system prompts to remain stable throughout a conversation for prompt caching.
The user keeps encrypted backups of persistent agent memory.
The user requires memory imports to resume safely after an interrupted process.
The user avoids dairy products when choosing meals.
The user likes travelling by train rather than taking short domestic flights.
The user edits Python source files in Visual Studio Code.
The plugin's supported Hermes host floor is release v0.21.5 (v2026.9.24).
Runtime dependencies include qdrant-client, httpx, and portalocker.
Deleting a memory removes its scoped live Qdrant point but does not erase SQLite event history or backups.
The local event and operation ledger can retain raw turns and prepared memory payloads; pending and failed payloads are needed for recovery.
The writer lease is a same-host local file lock, not a distributed lock for a shared collection across machines.
A turn enters the plugin's durable ledger only after the Hermes sync_turn callback begins and its SQLite transaction completes.
Hermes queues turn synchronization in memory before the provider callback, so a process exit before callback admission is outside the plugin's durability guarantee.
Prepared Qdrant mutations remain replayable after restart while their operation rows are pending.
Restoring an old backup can reintroduce memory data that was deleted from the live Qdrant collection.
